newsitem.title: ISRAEL: West Bank unrest flares again in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: West Bank unrest flares again in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops battled stone-throwing Palestinian protesters in Hebron on Friday as weeks of West Bank rage over Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem showed no sign of easing, witnesses said.

They said more than 400 Arab youths rained stones on Israeli troops at the confrontation line dividing Hebron into Israeli and Palestinian sectors. Soldiers responded with teargas and rubber coated metal bullets.
Hebron's Alia hospital said 16 Arabs were treated for rubber bullet injuries.
"Allahu Akbar (God is Greatest)," shouted one protester while hurling a Molotov cocktail towards Israeli troops. Six of the petrol bombs were hurled at soldiers but no one was hurt, witnesses said.
The army was checking the report.

Witnesses said Palestinian police commanders dispatched a Rapid Reaction Force, a special unit found only in Hebron, to disperse the protesters. PLO troops, waving short iron clubs, pressed rioters back.

The PLO took control of 80 percent of Hebron in January under an interim peace deal. Israeli troops remain in the rest of the city, holy to Moslems and Jews, to guard some 400 Jewish settlers in the town's heart.

Hebron has been the site of some of the fiercest clashes ignited last month when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967 and claimed by both sides.
Three Palestinians have been killed by Israeli soldiers and scores wounded in 16 consecutive days of unrest.

Three Israeli women were killed by a Palestinian suicide bomber in a Tel Aviv cafe two weeks ago. Two Islamic Jihad militants blew themselves up this week in a pair of botched suicide attacks in Gaza.
